You can buy frames rather cheap. wooden in the $10 range. If you intend to do white on black. I'd suggest I nice 110 mesh print flash print. If you want it to have a softer hand feel, use a 158 mesh. But nothing higher or you are going to work yourself to death.
I have an old and cheap speedball frame I used. I just wanted to see if I could make them myself and save a bit of money. If making them keeps being a pain in the ass I may just end up buying more.

I remember when I first started. I was in the same boat. When burning your screens make sure you don't over expose. That can cause as much and issue as under exposed. Are you using premixed emulsion on are you mixing the emulsion that comes with a small bottle of diazonium photogelatin?

edit* If you are coating your screens make sure you coat BOTH sides lightly. Thick emulsion is a pain in the ass to wash out and causes issues with expose times

I used some speedball emulsion where I mixed it myself. The results were pretty good. I had to scrub in a few spots but I think I was just being too gentle initially. Now that I think of it, it may have been too thick. Like I mentioned in the OP, I need to get a decent scoop coater.
